sources.title: AI capability is not the same as worker control
sources.observation: The synthesis separates access to AI capability from control over tasks, worker welfare, and successful remedy.
sources.mechanism: A tool can increase capability while decision rights, measurement, and correction remain with an employer or platform.
limits: This is a synthesis boundary, not a pooled causal estimate.

sources.title: Capability can arrive with dependence
sources.observation: The reader frames AI infrastructure as potentially building useful capability and dependence together, while keeping portability, exit, and state-control effects open.
sources.mechanism: A service can make work possible while increasing reliance on a provider or system that users cannot easily replace.
limits: The page preserves open questions about application migration, outcomes, portability, and exit.

sources.title: AI is changing which work remains scarce
sources.observation: The annual-report synthesis tracks AI as a force that can compress routine execution while increasing the value of distribution, judgment, accountability, and scarce expertise.
sources.mechanism: When routine work becomes cheap, value and bargaining power can move toward owners of distribution, context, judgment, and workflow control.
limits: This is a cross-company annual-report synthesis, not one company's measured AI outcome.

sources.title: AI can make routine execution cheaper while raising the value of strategy
sources.observation: The industry writeup describes AI website builders compressing template-based execution and shifting competition toward strategy, brand, personalization, and distribution.
sources.mechanism: Automation lowers the price of repeatable execution and can move scarce value toward higher-context work.
limits: The writeup combines industry estimates and company examples; each underlying measure needs source-level review before a general labor claim.

sources.title: AI demand creates a fast-growing infrastructure business
sources.observation: The Inc. 5000 record describes CoreWeave as a specialized GPU infrastructure provider serving AI labs, startups, and enterprises facing a shortage of compute.
sources.mechanism: A physical and financial infrastructure bottleneck can create a specialized layer that captures demand before AI becomes an ordinary workflow.
limits: The Inc. record identifies a growth hypothesis and revenue band; it does not prove customer benefit, durable margins, or AI productivity.

sources.title: AI work narratives need independent cultural measures
sources.observation: The Atlas thread places company-reported AI adoption beside editorial context, consumer measures, independent workplace measures, and an explicit open question about productivity and adoption.
sources.mechanism: A company narrative becomes more useful when it is compared with independent measures rather than treated as proof of an outcome.
limits: The thread explicitly says its sources do not establish productivity change, adoption scale, or causality.

sources.sourceLocator: FY2025 10-K and FY2026 Q1-Q3 direct SEC records
sources.title: C3.ai's report window shows what company records can and cannot prove
sources.observation: C3.ai's direct-record ledger covers the FY2025 10-K and three FY2026 10-Qs. It supports reported software, customer, accounting, deployment, risk, and financial facts, but does not independently measure accuracy, productivity, decision quality, privacy, worker conditions, or end-user outcomes.
sources.mechanism: A company's annual and quarterly reports can show commercial movement and stated deployments while leaving the lived result of an AI workflow unmeasured.
sources.reportingPeriod: FY2025 annual report plus FY2026 Q1, Q2, and Q3
limits: The report window does not identify an organization, model version, affected person, decision, input, output, error, override, appeal, remedy, or later outcome.

insight.title: AI can return time without returning control
insight.plainLanguageSummary: The current evidence supports a narrower reading than 'AI makes work more productive': AI can remove visible tasks while decisions, measurement, correction, and dependence remain controlled by an employer, platform, or infrastructure provider.
insight.strongestAlternative: The apparent control gap may be temporary because early deployments have not yet matured into stable workflow changes.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A compatible longitudinal study shows durable control, pay, and remedy improvements for affected workers.
Company and independent records show that workers can understand, correct, and leave AI-mediated decisions without material penalty.
insight.nextTest: Track one named AI-mediated workflow from company deployment through worker or customer use, correction, appeal, and exit evidence.
